targets.text: events-cli ships its second wave: the deferred arcs land on the first slice — the agentfront MCP+HTTP binding from the core registry (#6), durable identity-owned subscriptions with history and bounded cursor drain (#7), pipelines over the event graph (#8), shell-cli-routed stack verbs (#9), and dynsec identities with a documented remote-access opt-in (#10) — with issue #3 answered and closed

The wave announcement is honest only arc-by-arc: the exported spec marks #6/#8/#9/#10 as deferred with issue links and claims nothing delivered beyond the opening arc — mirroring how the first-slice spec carried its own deferred rows

Issue #3's two outstanding asks get an events-cli reply and the issue closes: the importable symbol is 'from events_cli import EventClient' (lazy PEP 562 re-export; events_cli.client defines it — their placeholder guess 'EventsClient' is one letter wrong and would degrade to a silent no-op), the constructor is EventClient(host='127.0.0.1', port=1883, *, client_id=..., connect=True) so connect() runs in the constructor by default, and the reTerminal bridge subscribes over raw loopback MQTT for this wave (client-side drain arrives with #7); acceptance is already recorded 10/10 in docs/acceptance/2026-07-24-issue-3-live-run.md

The reply posted on #3 names EventClient, its import path, the constructor signature, connect-in-constructor, and the raw-MQTT subscribe answer for the reTerminal bridge; the issue is closed after the reply (or explicitly left open by the operator with the reason stated)

Issue #9's reopen trigger has fired: shell-cli 0.13.x ships process.exec/process.shell behind a policy gate with persisted evidence records (its README Status section still claims no runner exists — stale against its own CHANGELOG), so the #9 evaluation of routing events up/down/logs/status through shell-cli is actionable now; any migration must keep StackError->CliError, exit code 2 for environment errors, and no traceback on stderr
The #9 evaluation runs during this wave and its verdict — migrate or stay on subprocess, with reasons — is recorded on issue #9, not silently dropped

Issue #7's cursor design must not assume total order on envelope ids: evt_ ids are Crockford ULIDs sortable at millisecond granularity only, with no intra-millisecond monotonicity (recorded on the events-first-slice frame) — the cursor must be store-assigned sequence, or the core must grow monotonic ids, before replay-from-cursor lands
A test mints two envelope ids in the same millisecond and proves drain order equals store append order and cursor resume is exact — no ordering is ever derived from comparing ULIDs

Issue #10's dynsec landing removes 'allow_anonymous true' from the generated mosquitto.conf — the template's own comment binds them ('when they land, this line goes away') — while keeping the anonymous co-located loopback path #3 depends on (REACHY_MQTT_URL=localhost:1883), and a stack-marked test must verify the dynsec plugin actually ships and initialises in eclipse-mosquitto:2.1.2-alpine (per_listener_settings is false, so auth settings are global)

Deferred-arc condition: when #10 lands, the regenerated template drops allow_anonymous true, a stack-marked test proves the dynsec path in eclipse-mosquitto:2.1.2-alpine, and the anonymous co-located loopback lane #3 depends on still works; until then this wave keeps anonymous loopback

The pyproject [project] description drift is fixed in the wave's first PR: it presently claims events-cli 'fronts it through agentfront as a CLI, an HTTP API and an MCP surface' in the present tense while #6 is unbuilt — prose ahead of code, exactly what CLAUDE.md's Known-drift rule exists for; reword to today's truth (or record in Known drift until #6 lands)
The pyproject description on main no longer claims MCP/HTTP surfaces exist; the rewording rides the arc's first PR with its version bump

The stable CLI contract survives every arc of the wave: _output.py stdout/stderr split and _errors.py exit codes stay frozen, the explain catalog keeps BOTH ('events',) and ('events-cli',) root keys, no traceback ever reaches stderr, and every new verb (watch, pipeline, dynsec-facing) goes through register(sub) plus a catalog entry with non-infinite --max/--timeout defaults — the rubric gate and pinned tests are the enforcement

The rubric gate (agentfront cli doctor --strict) and the pinned contract tests — dual catalog root keys, prog resolution, stdout/stderr split, exit codes — pass unchanged on every PR of the arc; enforcement is CI, not intention

docs/contract.md's 'What is built, and what is not' table is updated in the same PR as each arc that lands — it is currently honest (watch/pipeline verbs absent, dynsec listed 'not built — #10'), and keeping it honest is part of each arc's definition of done, not a trailing docs task
Each landing PR touches docs/contract.md's built/not-built table in the same change that adds the surface — a PR adding a verb without the table update does not merge

Consumers of the contract lane who need bounded, resumable consumption: agents draining events inside a turn (the MCP/HTTP shape #6 will derive later), humans and scripts on the events CLI, and services importing events_cli — first on spark-f8a9. Producer-owned raw trees (reachy/*) keep raw MQTT and are unaffected
The named consumers are real: the drain shape serves an agent turn within bounded time (proven by the --timeout tests), and reachy's raw-MQTT lane is untouched by the arc's diff

events-cli has a consume side: named durable subscriptions survive broker and consumer restarts; 'events watch <sub> --since <cursor> --max N --timeout S' returns a bounded batch plus a cursor with nothing acknowledged lost; 'events emit/get/list' round-trip envelope events through the contract lane; drained history lives in a store that survives stack restarts — #1's emit-and-watch acceptance items are met for the event plane

Every element of the after-state is mechanically checkable via the stack-marked suite: survive-restart, bounded drain, cursor resume, and the emit-to-watch round-trip — nothing rests on a judgment call

Today the fabric is publish-only: EventClient publishes, the reTerminal bridge subscribes over raw MQTT, and there is no subscribe/drain/history surface at all — 'events watch' does not exist, a contract-lane consumer that restarts loses everything published while it was away, and no store holds event history
The before-state is evidence, not narrative: at the pre-arc HEAD, events_cli contains no subscribe/consume/store code and no watch/emit/get/list/sub verb exists in the parser or the explain catalog

Stack-marked proof on spark-f8a9: create a subscription, publish N envelopes while no drainer is connected, restart the broker, then drain — all N arrive in order within --timeout with a cursor; resuming from that cursor returns nothing already acknowledged; a second CLI process watches what the first emits; the default pytest selection stays dockerless throughout
The success signal runs as an executable script or marked test on spark-f8a9 with observable output per item, exiting non-zero on any failure — a gate, not a demo, like scripts/acceptance-issue-3.sh

Durable subscriptions are MQTT persistent sessions, not a resident control service: 'events sub add <name> <pattern>' registers a broker-side persistent session (clean_start=false, QoS 1, session expiry effectively infinite) subscribed to the pattern's topic filter, so the broker's existing persistence (persistence true + volume + autosave 60) buffers the backlog while no drainer is connected — no always-on control-service container ships in this arc (the resident service becomes #8's concern when pipelines need active run advancement); the undrained-backlog bound (max_queued_messages) is set explicitly in the generated mosquitto.conf and documented

A stack-marked test proves the architecture: sub add, publish N envelopes with no drainer connected, docker restart of the broker, then drain returns all N in order — and the generated mosquitto.conf sets max_queued_messages explicitly with the bound documented in docs/contract.md

'events watch <sub> --since <cursor> --max N --timeout S' drains: resume the session, consume up to --max, append to the history store, acknowledge, return the batch plus the next cursor; defaults are non-infinite (--max 100, --timeout 30) and there is no unbounded --follow in this arc

A drain call returns within its --timeout with at most --max events plus a cursor; resuming from the returned cursor re-delivers nothing acknowledged; drain/cursor logic is tested pure and dockerless, the broker path behind the stack marker

'events emit <type> --data <file|->' validates through the core envelope (generated id/time) and publishes QoS 1 to the canonical topic via EventClient; 'events get <event-id>' and 'events list --type <t> --max N' read drained history from the store — every verb with --json, registered via register(sub) with catalog entries

Two CLI processes demonstrate the emit-to-watch round-trip on a live stack (stack-marked); get/list return drained envelopes by id and type with --json; envelope validation and store logic keep their coverage in the default dockerless selection

The canonical transport mapping is defined and documented in docs/contract.md: envelope events publish to 'events/<type with dots as topic-level separators>' and a subscription pattern like 'task.*' compiles to the matching MQTT filter — topic names stay a transport detail per #1, the dotted type stays the contract, and producer-owned trees stay outside the mapping

The type-to-topic and pattern-to-filter mapping is pure and tested dockerless in both directions; docs/contract.md documents it; and a test proves reachy/* topics are not captured by contract-lane subscription patterns

Every subscription records an owner identity as a declared name (default resolved from culture.yaml nick, falling back to the client id) — unauthenticated on loopback in this arc, forward-compatible with #10's dynsec so identity-owned subscriptions gain real authentication without a schema change
Every subscription record carries its owner; 'events sub list --json' shows it; and the record schema needs no migration when #10 lands (the dynsec identity name is the owner name)

This arc delivers #7 plus the riders (the #3 reply/close and the pyproject description fix) only: no agentfront MCP/HTTP (#6), no pipelines (#8), no shell-cli migration (#9 — its evaluation verdict is recorded on the issue separately), no dynsec (#10), no SSE/websocket streaming — each deferred arc lands per its own issue contract, mirroring the first-slice precedent
The arc's PRs add no agentfront-binding, pipeline, dynsec or SSE code; the deferred issues stay open with their contracts intact; the arc's diff contains no surface from #6/#8/#10

The stack-marked integration suite runs against an isolated scratch stack — its own compose project/container name, host port, volume and stack dir (EVENTS_STACK_DIR override) — and never restarts the production events-mosquitto, which serves the robot's nervous system live on this box; applying the template change (max_queued_messages) to the spark-f8a9 broker is a documented service window with rollback, like the first slice's cutover

The integration suite's setup provably targets its own compose project name, port and volume (asserted in the tests themselves), events-mosquitto's uptime is unbroken by a full suite run, and the live template rollout is recorded as a service window with a rehearsed rollback in docs/acceptance/

History captures only what a registered subscription's persistent session queued: events emitted before any subscription exists, or published at QoS 0, are transported but never captured — there is no global capture until #8's control service; docs/contract.md states this so no consumer assumes 'events list' is a complete log
docs/contract.md states the capture boundary in its own section, and a stack test proves an event published before 'sub add' is absent from a later drain while one published after is present

Backlog overflow semantics are documented from evidence, not assumption: mosquitto 2.1.2's default bound is 1000 queued messages per offline session and overflow drops the NEWEST messages silently (probe: 1200 published offline, exactly m00000-m00999 delivered in order; one broker log notice) — the template sets max_queued_messages explicitly, contract.md documents drop-newest, and the watch/drain docs point at 'events logs' for the drop notice

A stack test publishes bound+K messages to an offline subscription and proves exactly 'bound' oldest messages arrive in order; the template carries max_queued_messages with a comment stating drop-newest; contract.md documents it

Concurrent drains of one subscription are MQTT session takeover (the broker kicks the first drainer; observed and logged by the probe): persist-then-ack plus store dedupe on event id makes takeover lose nothing, and contract.md documents single-drainer-per-subscription semantics
A stack test starts drain A, starts drain B on the same subscription, and proves the store holds every event exactly once afterwards; contract.md documents single-drainer semantics

Durable capture requires QoS 1 publishes and the docs must say so: EventClient.publish AND publish_event default to qos=0, so an importable-client producer publishing envelopes with defaults silently bypasses durable capture — 'events emit' publishes qos=1 explicitly, and the client docstrings + contract.md state that QoS 0 bypasses capture
'events emit' passes qos=1 explicitly (unit-asserted); client.py docstrings and contract.md both state that QoS 0 publishes bypass durable capture

The history store is per-host like the stack itself: it lives beside the stack state (default_stack_dir's XDG convention, honouring an env override), never CWD-relative — 'events list' answers the same from any directory — and every stored record carries a store-format version marker so a future migration has something to key on
'events list' returns identical results from two different CWDs against the same host stack (test); stored records carry the format-version field from the first write

Subscription names and patterns are validated at the boundary: names are slugs, patterns use the dotted-type grammar with '*' only, and raw MQTT filter characters (#, +, /) are rejected with a field-level error — a pattern can never escape the events/ topic prefix
Unit tests reject '#', 'a/+', 'a/b', '../x' and empty patterns with field-level errors, dockerless; the compiled filter is always prefixed events/
